notes.title: Welcome to Taskforce v1.07
notes.content:
Hi Folks!

As with many of our other games this year, Taskforce has been updated today.

This is primarily an engine update, so there are no major gameplay changes, but a few things have changed in the background:
1. New mouse pointer and hi-red lens flares
2. Settings for expert users are now in Options.txt rather than Config.txt. There are two new options there: robustinit and fixaspect which can help fix video problems. See the Readme.txt for details.
3. Persistent settings and the saved games are now backed up the Steam Cloud.
4. The only gameplay change is that the Campaign Completed Achievement now requires that you must complete each mission at least once (on any skill level), then the final mission.

Happy playing.

Mark

notes.title: Flatspace Updated
notes.content:
Greetings Starpilots!

Flatspace has had an upgrade and overhaul to match the capabilities of Flatspace IIk, and other new games like Gunstorm.

This is primarily an engine update, so there are no gameplay changes, but a lot has changed in the background, such as:
-New fonts, new lens flares, new starfield, and much better screen aspect support and improved graphics set-up.
-New separation of expert user options in Options.txt and game settings. Graveyard and settings are now stored in the Steam Cloud.
-Controls now support a full keyboard and (for future games!) 4 or more game controllers.

You'll notice a few things:
1. New fonts. The heading is less blurry and smaller on 16:9 screens, and the main font is better spaced.
2. New settings for expert users in Options.txt. There are two new options there: robustinit and fixaspect, plus fixes and upgrades to basic settings like screen resolution and timers.
3. Persistent settings and the graveyard are now backed up the Steam Cloud.
4. Better aspect-ratio support. The old 4:3 game is now transformed and looks largely the same at the 16:9 game. For other screens, the aspect can be fixed to stretch it if needed so that Flatspace should be playable on any shape or size of screen.
5. New starfield, new mouse pointer, new lens flares.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1210780/Flatspace/

Mark

notes.title: Taskforce Updated
notes.content:
Greetings Strategy Fans! Welcome to the first Taskforce update in over a year. Quite a few changes in this one...

FIRST! The campaign is now fully unlocked so you can play any mission in any order. This is quite a radical change but instantly improves the game. The original Amiga Taskforce from 1994, and Hilt II, both allowed any mission to be chosen. All of the training missions are available from the start too. Doing this avoids any worries or annoyances about losing campaign progress, and instantly adds a lot to the game for new buyers.

Secondly, Steam Achievements have been added, as current players will see in their Steam pages. There are lots of possibilities here, so there's an Achievement for completing each mission on each difficulty, and one for each training mission on Elite (some are harder than others!). There is an Achievement for completing the last mission and defeating Morgane (on any difficulty), but this is (ironically) easier than some of the others and will probably be superseded one day...

3. (I'll switch to numbers now): The Config.txt file is now loaded/saved to the game main folder rather than using the Windows 'Documents' folder, because Windows complains about security when looking in Documents. This shouldn't make any difference to players.

4. The screenwidth/screenheight/adapter options in the Config.txt now work, they didn't before, it was a bug. So you can at last set a custom screen mode.

And that's it apart from minor updates to the code. The demo includes the new features too. Thanks to the people who have bought the game in the past year, this update happened because of your sales. Find Taskforce here:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1291150/Taskforce_The_Mutants_of_October_Morgane/

Enjoy!

Mark

notes.title: Welcome to Taskforce v1.06

Enjoy!

notes.title: Taskforce Dev Update: Training Testing
notes.content:
A few tweaks to the game today and testing the new training missions. All have new objectives. The Assassination Training involves hunting one enemy but not being allowed to kill anyone except your target. It's perfect for one, lone unit, hiding behind objects and using stealth tactics. The opposite end is the Major Assault, one of the few missions in the game which allows you to use all 12 members of the squad. In this, an overwhelming force, more than 3:1, have taken over your base and you must retake it.

Testing is taking place each day. We're at the stage now where radical new ideas are for potential sequels. The key thing now is to check that what is there, and what should be there, works exactly as it should.

Most of the training missions make use of multiple levels to provide interesting vantage points. This Terror Troop armed with a Pyrox Burner is one of 40 enemies here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37538589/7c8cd286d5c275a1b310539a68d93ae2856f3b71.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Taskforce Dev Update: Teuton Arcanum
notes.content:
Great progress on Taskforce. You can see all new screenshots of the latest build on the store today. I can now introduce Teuton Arcanum, the organisation you will command in the game.

The Teuton Arcanum Special Knight Force, known as Taskforce, is a global organisation, founded in the 9th century in Aachen, Germany, by executive order of Emperor Charlemagne. It originally consisted of nine trusted knights, and indeed even today it is led by the 'Nine Unknown Knights'; unknown because even the Knights themselves do not know the real identities of the other members.

The organisation has survived until today, and is now based in a underground city beneath the Swiss Alps known as The Cathedral. Their symbol is the Arcanum Knot, a nine pointed star, and each point represents one of the Nine Unknown Knights and the different departments which they administer: Archival, Scientific, Esoteric, Political, Active Scientific and Practical Operations (ASPO makes all of your equipment), Sentinel, Financial, Military, and the Dark Order.

In the game you will command Knight Force One, twelve of the 169 troops in the Military wing.

notes.title: Taskforce Dev Update: New Graphics System
notes.content:
A huge few weeks for Taskforce. A week ago I decided to reprogram the graphics system entirely, which needed new versions of the 400-or-so objects in the game. At the same time, I thought I'd create new textures at double the existing resolution too, so effectively all of the terrain graphics have been recreated in the past, long and exhausting, week.

Now, blocks and wall sections are correctly sealed, effectively automatically creating tubes of polygons for the walls and windows etc. Before, almost all objects showed strange fragments of polygons, holes, gaps. Everything looked like an error, but was there for speed. Now it's probably faster and looks better. Here is a look:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37538589/789b2e5cec51087a90790055d809f0e7bf3c275f.jpg[/img]

Those concrete-ends are just the unseen walls, the black holes will be filled in when your troops see them, as normal. One other thing is that you can now shoot through windows, which looks great and allows proper S.A.S. style entry into buildings.

All of this work means that, sadly, I won't be able to make the deadline for the Steam Summer Games Festival. A public demo will appear, but not this week. Due to the busy-ness of Steam's June Fest, the release date for Taskforce might be pushed back to the end of July.

One last note is that now that all of the graphics are new, the existing screenshots and the video are effectively invalid. I will create new ones...

notes.title: Taskforce Dev Update: Commando Fun
notes.content:
Huge updates to Taskforce today. I've added the ability to skip units which have moved, and restricted movement on top of odd tiles, like walking over pot-plants, this was actually possible! I've also added a lot more music options. Oddly, for me, there isn't much music in this game; I'd like to add more but time is so limited.

At least five of the missions have had big changes to the maps. I want to make everything non-linear, so that players are given a target but can do it in so many ways that there is no right or wrong or best way. In this mission, a tiny commando-style raid has been authorised; you take just 4 units and must enter a building at night with the aim of destroying a cluster of generators. You are massively outnumbered by armed guards, so must evade as much as possible. There are so many ways in and out of the building that you are free to choose. You can even walk right over the roof and enter the target zone itself without so much as a single guard. All a far cry from linear F.P.S. games with a start here and a target at the end of the hall, but of course, no route is necessarily best, and, just as in [i]The Guns of Navarone[/i], you must escape after the bombs go off.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37538589/fe038bef7424845a3fb73ad33068a7f355fe55d2.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Taskforce Dev Update: Training Missions
notes.content:
Working hard today on new training missions. These are a big part of the game, each new unlocked mission also unlocks training missions, allowing you to face enemies in a sort of holodeck environment. I'm designing new maps for each type of training. My golden rule is to give the player options. These games are more like multiplayer F.P.S. games than most single player games. Every game different, with so many options and missions to choose from that you can play again and again and never have the same experience.

Here's a look at the one of them in testing (no secrets to which!) - the special thing about this one is that your team starts separated, and in a different place each time you play.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37538589/a7efdf66eaa945bbd5409516c1d6fcbdb0cb5387.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Taskforce Dev Update: Random Items
notes.content:
Lots of work on Taskforce today. Added the ability for items to have random starts for missions that demand the retrieval of objects. Random starts were always in place for enemies, this is so important to keep the game fresh and non-linear. This same facility for items should add the same level of sparkle.

I'll post regular updates on testing and the game progress, moving towards the release date in June. Here are a couple of Secret Files in one of the Training Missions.
